title: Preparing for Canada's High Impact Start-up Pilot: Four Things That Hold Under Any Rules
excerpt: Nobody knows the pilot's criteria. A founder can still prepare: four things the old programme asked for and any successor will almost certainly ask for too.
keyTakeaway: Preparation that does not depend on the final rules: dated evidence of traction, a clean cap table, a language result timed to the opening, and a plan that does not rest on one door.
summaryEn: Four preparations for a founder waiting on the High Impact Start-up Pilot, drawn from what the old Start-up Business Class assessed and what IRCC has hinted about the new one.

faq.q: Can I start preparing before the criteria are published?
faq.a: Yes, for things that mattered under the old rules and will likely matter again: evidence of traction, clean ownership and a language result. None of it is a reservation.

content:
This is for a founder who runs a real company and is deciding what to do with the months before the pilot opens. The honest framing: you cannot prepare for criteria that do not exist. You can prepare for the things any entrepreneur programme has to check. IRCC's only hint about the pilot's test is "elite entrepreneurs" and, in the trade press's reading, measurable economic impact. Checked 5 November 2026.

1. Evidence of traction, kept dated

Revenue, signed customers, usage and product milestones, each with a date and where it came from. If the test is impact, then impact is something you show, not something you describe. Keep it in a form someone outside the company can verify.

2. A clean cap table and a real company

The old programme looked hard at structure. Each applicant needed at least 10% of the voting rights, applicants and the designated organization together needed more than 50%, and investments had to be equity, not convertible debt. IRCC, assessing the application The pilot may differ, but founder agreements, IP assigned to the company and funds you can trace are the same homework either way.

3. A language result that will not expire

The old programme asked for CLB 5 in all four skills from a test taken under two years before filing. Expect the pilot to ask for at least that, and time the test to the opening, not before it. A result that expires while IRCC is still drafting is money spent twice.

4. A plan that does not rest on one door

The pilot has no opening date. We expect 2027, which is our inference. A founder who must move this year needs a plan that works if that is wrong. Compare the routes open today and treat the pilot as upside, not as the plan.

What not to do

Do not pay anyone to reserve a place. Nothing can be reserved, because nothing has been published to reserve against.

A one-page evidence log

The simplest useful tool is a single document that a stranger could audit. One row per claim, four columns:

ClaimDateSourceWhere the proof is
Signed customerWhen the contract was signedContract or signed orderThe file or folder
Monthly revenueThe monthBank or payment-processor statementThe exported statement
Product milestoneRelease dateRelease notes or repository historyThe link or the file
OwnershipDate of the last changeCap table and shareholder agreementThe signed documents

It costs a few hours now and saves weeks when a programme finally asks. It also makes one thing obvious early: which of your claims you can prove and which you only believe.

Our pilot page lists what IRCC has stated and what is still blank, and we update it whenever IRCC publishes.
